correctness.rationale: For every stated n,k the two-dimensional Fourier block M_j has simple eigenvalues and all eigenvectors nonzero on the outer ring. Each lambda-eigenspace is spanned by distinct Fourier columns indexed by J_lambda. The first |J_lambda| outer rows are a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix; PBH gives controllability for r=max |J|, and eigenvalue multiplicity gives the matching lower bound. Chebyshev polynomial degree establishes 2k+2 cap. The n=11 resultant is recomputed exactly using integer operations, and squarefreeness follows from its derivative modulo 2; full finite Kalman ranks are checked over a prime field.

value.rationale: Provides an explicit globally minimum actuator count and placement throughout an infinite two-parameter family where the spectral lower bound is not automatically attainable for generic graphs. It is meaningful beyond code: GP(11,2) needs just two independent fixed-Laplacian inputs, contrasted with its known six-vertex zero-forcing requirement; the exact rule addresses the motivated gap between spectral and robust combinatorial placement.
